provenance_note: Every case is generated by a seeded numpy expression recorded in 'generator'. None of it is captured traffic. A detection rate measured here describes this organ against these expressions, not against attackers.
positive_definition: Sessions that share a single behaviour direction the rest of the population does not, i.e. a botnet whose members are driven by the same controller.
negative_definition: Sessions from independent humans, and (deliberately) homogeneous fleets, whose shared direction is caused by identical configuration rather than by a controller. The homogeneous-fleet cases are the hard ones: they are the reason this organ cannot be scored honestly by a single number.

cases.label: benign
cases.generator: 30 clean fleet devices and 10 'compromised' ones drawn from the IDENTICAL law: outer(N(0,6),[1,0,0,0,0]) + N(0,0.05)
cases.rationale: IDENTIFIABILITY CONTROL, not a detection case. The label is bookkeeping only. This case asks whether ANY statistic on the session x feature matrix could separate the two groups when both are drawn from the same law. If not, a miss here is not a detector fault and must be excluded from the published rate rather than counted against it.

cases.rationale: A botnet hiding inside a legitimate shared direction. The obvious rank-1 signal is already present in the benign population, so the discriminator has to be a scale difference, not a variance share.
